A_target.statement:
Let $\mathbf A$ be a real $n \times n$ [[Definition:Matrix|matrix]].
Then $\mathbf A = \mathbf Q \mathbf P$ with $\mathbf Q$ [[Definition:Orthogonal Matrix|orthogonal]] and $\mathbf P$ [[Definition:Symmetric Matrix|symmetric]] [[Definition:Positive Semidefinite Matrix|positive semidefinite]], where $\mathbf P = \sqrt {\mathbf A^\intercal \mathbf A}$ is unique.

B_source.statement:
Let $\mathbf A$ be a real matrix.
Then $\mathbf A = \mathbf U \mathbf \Sigma \mathbf V^\intercal$ with $\mathbf U$, $\mathbf V$ orthogonal and $\mathbf \Sigma$ diagonal with non-negative entries.

substitutions.the singular value decomposition: a regrouping of its three factors

object_map.reformulation: Insert V^T V = I into the SVD and regroup into a rotation times a stretch.

validity_conditions: The positive semidefinite square root of a PSD matrix is unique.
The orthogonal factor is unique when A is invertible.
proof_plan: By the [[Singular Value Decomposition]], $\mathbf A = \mathbf U \mathbf \Sigma \mathbf V^\intercal = \paren {\mathbf U \mathbf V^\intercal} \paren {\mathbf V \mathbf \Sigma \mathbf V^\intercal}$.
$\mathbf Q = \mathbf U \mathbf V^\intercal$ is orthogonal, as a product of orthogonal matrices.

$\mathbf P = \mathbf V \mathbf \Sigma \mathbf V^\intercal$ is symmetric, and $\mathbf x^\intercal \mathbf P \mathbf x = \paren {\mathbf V^\intercal \mathbf x}^\intercal \mathbf \Sigma \paren {\mathbf V^\intercal \mathbf x} \ge 0$.
